why: I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 tests only `exit 1` and empty stdout. The stderr greps run there are used only in Check 2. Check 2 tests `bad config:`, the exact path, and line 3 / column 3, and it accepts any clear wording for the location. Check 3 tests only that the call throws and that the message includes the path (`OK` vs `RETURNED`/`NO PATH`). Check 4 requires `listening on 9000`, exit 0, and a deepEqual against `{ port: 9000 }`. Its "any other stdout" reads as stdout that differs from the expected line, which the expect line covers. Check 5 requires `# fail 0` at the head and at least one path-asserting test that is `not ok` on the base. The stricter items are under "Advisory (not pass/fail)": whether line and column are computed by the repo, swallowed errors, ENOENT changes, and absolute paths. No PASS or FAIL condition adds an extra requirement.
